title: Aging and house prices
summary_en: Demographics shape the housing market in slow-burning ways. Takáts uses cross-country panel data to show that ageing populations exert a measurable downward pull on real house prices: as the share of working-age population falls relative to retirees, demand for owner-occupation declines and house-price growth slows. The paper provides a quantitative estimate of the demographic drag on real house prices and projects how it will play out across major OECD economies over coming decades.
data_used: Cross-country panel of OECD economies covering several decades, with national house-price indices, demographic shares (working-age vs. retired), and standard housing-market controls (interest rates, income, urbanisation). Panel fixed-effects estimation with country and year effects.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian housing and pension policy (BM lakáspolitika, NGM, MNB Pénzpiaci Tanács): Hungary's projected demographic ageing implies a multi-decade headwind to real house-price growth, with knock-on effects on household-wealth distribution and on the calibration of macroprudential housing-market rules. Provides a quantitative benchmark for stress-testing long-run housing-market scenarios in Hungarian central-bank reports.
